title: Trump: Bodyguards for Azerbaijani president, in town for Trump’s Board of Peace, attack protesters in DC
description_short: Trump: Bodyguards for Azerbaijani president, in town for Trump’s Board of Peace, attack protesters in DC
description_medium: Bodyguards for Azerbaijani president, in town for Trump’s Board of Peace, attack protesters in DC. Demonstrators were outside hotel in Washington demanding the release of political prisoners in Azerbaijan This entry is cataloged as a standalone event because it captures a concrete action, public statement, or policy consequence linked directly to Trump. The downstream effects include elevated institutional stress, public-trust erosion, and measurable accountability pressure across affected systems.
description_long: Protesters in Washington said they were attacked by members of Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev’s security detail while he was in the city for a meeting of Donald Trump’s Board of Peace. The demonstrators had gathered outside the Waldorf Astoria hotel to call for the release of political prisoners in Azerbaijan. The Washington Post reported that the incident took place as the group approached Aliyev’s motorcade and that police referred a matter involving Azerbaijani security guards to the State Department. The allegations were not a finding by a court, and the public account did not establish what instructions the guards received or whether all participants were identified. The visit placed the protest in the context of a high-profile diplomatic gathering convened by Trump, but the reported assault was attributed to the visiting president’s security personnel, not to U.S. officials. The episode drew attention to how political dissent was treated around an international event on U.S. soil and to the diplomatic sensitivity of an alleged attack involving a foreign leader’s protective detail. The source-backed description keeps the protesters’ account and the police referral distinct from any unresolved investigation.

title: Trump White House voices opposition after Israel unveils plan to increase control over West Bank
description_short: Trump White House voices opposition after Israel unveils plan to increase control over West Bank
description_medium: Trump White House voices opposition after Israel unveils plan to increase control over West Bank. Israel’s security cabinet has approved plans that pave the way for more settlements in the occupied Palestinian territory This entry is cataloged as a standalone event because it captures a concrete action, public statement, or policy consequence linked directly to Trump. The downstream effects include elevated institutional stress, public-trust erosion, and measurable accountability pressure across affected systems.
description_long: After Israel’s security cabinet approved steps expanding Israeli control in the occupied West Bank, the Trump White House publicly opposed annexation. The Guardian reported that the measures included allowing Israeli Jews to purchase West Bank land directly and extending Israeli authority into areas where the Palestinian Authority exercises power. They did not require additional Israeli approval to take effect, although the report said the timing was unclear. Axios separately reported that Trump told it, “I am against annexation,” without commenting on the specifics of the cabinet decision. A White House official said a stable West Bank supported Israel’s security and the administration’s goal of regional peace. The episode showed a gap between Trump’s stated opposition to annexation and the Israeli government’s policy steps, which critics characterized as movement toward de facto annexation. The reporting does not say Israel formally annexed the territory or that Washington imposed consequences. It records a diplomatic position and an Israeli policy change whose practical effects were still developing. Keeping those distinctions clear avoids treating a stated objection as a reversal of the underlying measures.

title: Trump: ‘It’s discrimination’: US Small Business Administration cuts off loans to immigrant entrepreneurs
description_short: Trump: ‘It’s discrimination’: US Small Business Administration cuts off loans to immigrant entrepreneurs
description_medium: ‘It’s discrimination’: US Small Business Administration cuts off loans to immigrant entrepreneurs. Green card holders are now ineligible for loans through the SBA as agency carries out Trump’s ‘America First’ agenda This entry is cataloged as a standalone event because it captures a concrete action, public statement, or policy consequence linked directly to Trump. The downstream effects include elevated institutional stress, public-trust erosion, and measurable accountability pressure across affected systems.
description_long: The Small Business Administration changed its eligibility rules so lawful permanent residents could no longer receive SBA loans. The Guardian reported that the policy was announced in February 2026 and took effect for direct SBA loans in March, with SBA-backed loans subject to the restriction beginning in April. Under the new rule, a business with even partial ownership by a green-card holder could be excluded. The Associated Press reported that the SBA had approved 3,358 loans in fiscal 2025 to businesses partly owned by permanent residents, about 4% of the agency’s 85,000 approvals. Advocates said the restriction could reduce access to capital for immigrant entrepreneurs and affect hiring and local business growth. The administration presented the change as part of an “America First” approach under SBA administrator Kelly Loeffler. The measure changed federal loan access; it did not prohibit immigrant entrepreneurs from starting businesses or borrowing from every private lender. Its immediate practical reach depended on ownership structure and the type of SBA financing sought. The reporting documents a policy shift and its potential effects, while the broader economic impact remained uncertain.

title: Trump-Era Election Lies Crept Back Through a Puerto Rico Voting-Machine Conspiracy
description_short: Trump-Era Election Lies Crept Back Through a Puerto Rico Voting-Machine Conspiracy
description_medium: The Guardian reported that Tulsi Gabbard's testimony about seizing voting machines in Puerto Rico raised fresh questions about an old Venezuela-themed conspiracy theory tied to Trump's 2020 election lies. This is how poisoned ideas stay alive: they do not disappear, they get laundered through officials, hearings, and new jurisdictions. The costume changes; the fraud stays stupid.
description_long: Tulsi Gabbard told Congress in March 2026 that her office had obtained voting machines from Puerto Rico at the request of the U.S. attorney there. The Guardian reported that the prosecutor’s office had been drawn into efforts by Trump supporters to revive a long-discredited theory linking Venezuela to Trump’s 2020 election defeat. Gabbard described the inquiry as an effort to examine possible vulnerabilities; she did not publicly connect it to the Venezuela claims. Reuters had earlier reported that Gabbard’s office investigated Puerto Rico voting systems with the FBI after claims of Venezuelan hacking, but the probe produced no clear evidence of Venezuelan interference. The juxtaposition raised questions about how an old election conspiracy returned through official channels and a new jurisdiction. It does not show that the machines were altered, that Venezuela interfered, or that Gabbard endorsed the conspiracy. The source-backed issue is the seizure and testing of voting equipment, the stated justification, and the earlier conspiracy campaign around the prosecutor’s office. Those distinctions separate a documented investigative action from allegations that the investigation itself had not substantiated.

title: An Election Conspiracy Theorist Had Trump's Ear on Voting Laws and the Midterms
description_short: An Election Conspiracy Theorist Had Trump's Ear on Voting Laws and the Midterms
description_medium: The Guardian reported that election conspiracy theorist Peter Ticktin had Trump's ear on voting laws and midterm strategy, pushing ideas experts said could sharply restrict voting rights. The danger here is structural. Fringe delusion does not stay fringe once it gets a direct line to presidential power and a chance to harden into law.
description_long: Peter Ticktin, a Florida lawyer who represents some 2020 election deniers and has ties to Trump, urged the president to intervene in election administration before the 2026 midterms. The Guardian reported that Ticktin promoted an emergency executive order and shared a 17-page draft that would require voters to re-register with proof of citizenship, end mail voting and vote-tabulation machines, and require hand-counting of ballots. Ticktin argued that declaring an election emergency would give Trump authority to impose national rules. The proposed order was a draft and advocacy effort, not a policy that had taken effect. Election administration is primarily carried out by states, and any attempt to change the rules by executive order would face legal challenges. The article described concerns that the proposal could sharply restrict access to voting and concentrate control over election procedures in the federal executive. It also makes clear that Ticktin’s access and influence did not establish that Trump had accepted the draft or would issue it. The event is significant as an effort to bring a fringe election theory into presidential decision-making, while the outcome remained uncertain.
